findings.text: The `check_rules.py` assertion only checks `contains`, so a `FAST … check_rules.py …` or `SKIP … check_rules.py …` line would satisfy it even if the full plan stopped planning the self-check. Require the matched line to start with `PLAN` (the fast plan's `FAST` text names `check_rules.py`), so the test actually guards the full plan.
findings.title: Tighten full-plan assertion for rules check

findings.text: The fast banner still starts with the exact token sequence `GATE: PASS`, and a fast run exits 0 while `clippy -D warnings`, the external corpora, and the review-rule checks did not run. The repo's own idiom for recognizing a green gate is a substring match (`tests/baseline.rs` and `tests/projection.rs` both assert `contains("GATE: PASS")`), and any CI/wrapper doing the same cannot distinguish this from the merge verdict — which defeats the stated intent that the fast banner is "never the plain one". Use a prefix that does not contain `GATE: PASS` so every prefix/substring consumer sees a distinct verdict.
findings.title: maintainability

findings.text: The flag is only recognized as `$1`, so `scripts/check.sh baseline --fast` falls through to the `baseline [file]` handling and treats `--fast` as a filename instead of the documented usage error (exit 2); `plan --fast` is also rejected. Extract `--fast` from any position before parsing the step, then let the existing step validation reject it beside `baseline`/`decision`.
findings.title: Parse fast flag in any position
findings.code:
fast=0
if [ "${1:-}" = "--fast" ]; then
  fast=1
  shift
fi

findings.text: In fast mode this prints `FAST` even when `cargo-clippy` is absent, contradicting the comment that the tooling is present and hiding a missing dependency. Gate the fast branch on the same probe (while retaining the `dry` bypass for `plan`) so a missing tool still reports `SKIP`; apply the same pattern to the review-rule/review-scope branches.
findings.title: Report missing tooling in fast mode
findings.code:
if [ "$fast" -eq 1 ]; then
  fastskip "clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"
elif [ "$dry" -eq 1 ] || command -v cargo-clippy >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  run cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
else
  skip "clippy not installed (rustup component add clippy)"
fi

findings.text: This PR introduces three different figures for the same `--fast` measurement: this usage comment says "85s -> ~60s", the external-corpora comment a few lines later repeats "~19s of an 85s run", while AGENTS.md and the PR description state "a warm full run is 59s and a fast one 25s". A reader who quotes the gate's timing (which this repository treats as evidence, not decoration) gets two mutually exclusive answers. The likely cause is that the 85s/~60s pair predates the final measurement and was not updated; if so, the script comments should be aligned to 59s/25s (or both numbers should be stated with their provenance: cold vs warm). This is a documentation accuracy issue only; the flag behaves correctly.
findings.title: Contradictory measurements

findings.text: This test only drives `--fast plan`, which exits 3 and takes the `dry` branch of `finish()`. The load-bearing new path is the non-plan fast run: it must exit 0, print the FAST banner (not the plain one), and skip the four checks. A regression that reverted the fast PASS banner to the plain text, or that made a fast run fail unconditionally, would leave this suite green (the plan assertions still pass because `fastskip` runs in plan mode too). The `script_fixture`/`script_banner` harness defined below this test can already drive the copied script to its banner with a stub `cargo`; add a run there (copying `.req/variants` into the fixture so the release step is green) asserting exit 0, the fast banner, the `FAST` lines, and that the dropped `cargo clippy` / corpus / review-rule commands were not executed.
findings.title: test
